extracted.intended_audience: historians, ethnographers, and historical demographers studying California delta indigenous populations
extracted.subtask_description: Reconstructing and estimating aboriginal village and tribal population sizes in the Sacramento–San Joaquin delta using missionary baptism records, explorers' accounts, house counts, sex/age definitions, and contextual historical events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mission baptism records as demographic data / lower bound
rubrics_metrics.description: Mission books and baptism records provide counts of converts from particular rancherias and are used as documentary evidence of population presence and minimum size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat baptisms as a firm lower limit for population; where appropriate add baptized numbers to field estimates (e.g., "Merely adding the 200 missionized natives would bring the population estimate for the Bolbones up to 1,500"). In some cases the author doubles baptisms to approximate aboriginal population (e.g., 185 baptisms → aboriginal population ≈ 400).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust for differing missionary age/sex definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Franciscans and individual observers used different cutoffs for 'children' and for who was counted as male; these definitional differences materially affect population proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the correct age/sex scheme when converting partial counts to totals: example — Franciscans called children all persons under ten (not seven), and Zalvidea counted as men males between seven and forty; with proper correction men and women each contributed 41.8% and children 16.4%, so a village with 200 men would contain 563 persons in all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use house counts × persons-per-house to estimate population
rubrics_metrics.description: When house counts are available, multiply by an estimated persons-per-house figure to infer village size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate persons per house from descriptions and comparisons (example: 60 houses → average 9.38 persons per house; Chuppumne with 35 houses and house diameters ~43 ft could accommodate ~9 persons ⇒ population ≈315). Use architectural dimensions and typical household sizes to justify the multiplier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat explorers'/combatant estimates skeptically and adjust numerically
rubrics_metrics.description: Contemporary accounts often give exaggerated counts of enemy forces or village sizes; the author recommends critical reduction of such figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply skeptical reductions where motive for exaggeration exists (example: Soto's estimate of 1,000 warriors was judged excessive and "may be cut in half" to 500). Justify adjustments by cross-checking with logistical plausibility and other records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infer total population from warrior counts via assumed non-fighting male proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use reported numbers of warriors to infer the broader male population and then the total population using established percentage distributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for non-fighting males (young boys, invalids, old men). Example: 500 warriors → allow ~300 non-fighting males → male population ≈800; apply previously established sex/age percentages to estimate mean village size (author estimated ~475 from this method).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate by tribal complexes when individual village data are scarce
rubrics_metrics.description: Group settlements by tribal/nomenclatural affiliation (rather than strictly geographic points) to compute totals when documentary evidence names groups more reliably than precise localities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow a uniform tribal nomenclature (the author follows Schenck) and sum available estimates/convert counts across the tribal complex (example: Bolbones complex summed to 2,500 total and average village size slightly over 300).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume an average village size (~300) in absence of contrary evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no specific data exist for a given rancheria, use a baseline average village size for the delta region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author argues that "300 cannot be regarded as an excessive estimate for the average village of the delta" and applies this default unless clear reason exists to adopt a different value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for effects of raids, warfare, disease, and mission removals on observed counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that baptisms and later records reflect population after substantial disturbance; estimates of aboriginal (pre-contact or pre-raid) populations must account for attrition and removals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust upward from observed post-contact figures to reconstruct earlier populations (examples: Leuchas conversions after punitive expeditions reduced numbers; 396 baptisms of Aguastos interpreted as comprising substantially the entire tribe at conversion). Consider casualties, displacement, and capture when reconciling baptism totals with assumed aboriginal sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use temporal patterns of baptisms and diary entries to infer movements and geographic attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Clustering of conversion dates and first-appearance of village names in mission books can indicate geographic shifts, exhaustion of nearby populations, or the arrival of new groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze baptism dates to separate earlier local groups from later arrivals (example: conversions in 1777 were local peninsula rancherias; names appearing prior to 1800 as 'otra banda' indicate east-bay villages; a flood of new names after 1800 indicates movement into the delta approaches). Use this to assign baptisms to likely locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference expedition diaries, distance statements, and modern maps to locate settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use explorers' journals, noted distances/leagues, and contemporary scholarly maps (e.g., Schenck, Kroeber) to place rancherias when mission records are confused about localities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconcile inconsistent distance estimates (e.g., Duran's exaggerations vs Argueello's miles), interpret qualitative locality descriptors (e.g., 'remate', 'orilla del estero') and prefer concordant evidence across multiple sources to fix settlement locations and thus inform population aggregation.
